name: Nordic Modern
description: Nordic Modern — Scandinavian clarity, nature-inspired restraint, and functional warmth from the design traditions of Denmark, Sweden, Finland, and Norway

foundation.story: Nordic Modern design emerged in the 1950s from the intersection of Bauhaus functionalism and Scandinavian craft traditions. Designers like Alvar Aalto, Arne Jacobsen, and Marimekko proved that mass-produced objects could carry warmth and humanity. The palette draws from fjords, birch forests, lichen-covered granite, and the long blue twilight of northern latitudes.
foundation.philosophy: Lagom (just the right amount) — democratic beauty through restraint and natural materials

seedColors.name: Fjordblå
seedColors.tradition: The deep blue-grey of Norwegian fjord water at midday. A defining color of Scandinavian textiles and ceramics from Røros to Fiskars.

seedColors.name: Bjørkehvit (Birch White)
seedColors.tradition: The warm white of birch bark and unbleached Nordic linen. Never pure white — always carrying the warmth of natural fiber.
seedColors.source: Nordic Light: Modern Scandinavian Architecture, Henry Plummer

seedColors.name: Mosegrønn (Moss Green)
seedColors.tradition: The muted green of forest-floor moss and lichen. Present in Finnish ryijy rugs and Danish functionalist interiors.
seedColors.source: Finnish Design: A Concise History, Pekka Korvenmaa

seedColors.name: Multebær (Cloudberry)
seedColors.tradition: The amber-gold of ripe cloudberries (Rubus chamaemorus), a prized arctic fruit. This warm accent breaks the cool Nordic palette.

seedColors.name: Granitt (Granite)
seedColors.tradition: Norwegian granite grey. The foundation stone of Nordic architecture from stave churches to Sverre Fehn's modernist pavilions.
seedColors.source: New Nordic Architecture & Identity, Kjeld Kjeldsen

seedColors.name: Nordlys (Northern Light)
seedColors.tradition: Teal-green of the aurora borealis, captured in Marimekko prints and Finnish glass by Kaj Franck and Tapio Wirkkala.
seedColors.source: Scandinavian Design: An Introduction, David McFadden
